L'adenocarcinoma colorettale nasce quasi:
Colorectal adenocarcinoma almost always arises from an adenoma. The criterion for malignancy is invasion of the submucosa: in the colon, carcinoma confined to the mucosa does not metastasise. The T stage depends on depth (T1 submucosa, T2 muscularis propria, T3 subserosa/pericolic fat, T4 serosa or adjacent organs).
Radiological correlation: on CT asymmetric wall thickening or an “apple-core” mass; CT does not distinguish T1 from T2, but shows extension into the pericolic fat (T3), lymph nodes and liver and lung metastases. In right-sided colon cancer, iron-deficiency anaemia is the typical presentation.
Adenoma → carcinoma: lo decide l'invasio: Adenoma → carcinoma: submucosal invasion decides, not the grade of dysplasia.
